key_insight: CB-COMIL explains melanoma immunotherapy-response predictions through four supervised concepts, but these learned concepts are not interchangeable with measured biological values.
clinical_relevance: This research could support more interpretable immunotherapy-response prediction, but it does not establish readiness for treatment decisions.
method: Analyzes multiplex immunofluorescence whole-slide images using a concept bottleneck model.
Uses immune:tumour ratio, CD8/SOX10 balance, CD68 relative signal and PD-L1 evasion index.
Decomposes each prediction exactly into concept contributions.
evidence_signal: Developed on 211 slides and independently tested on 42, CB-COMIL achieved macro-F1 0.69 versus 0.67 for an opaque comparator (difference 0.020; 95% CI −0.103 to 0.144).
watch_item: Although learned concepts correlated with measured counterparts (Spearman ρ 0.61–0.76), substituting measurements reduced macro-F1 from 0.68 to 0.48 in 41 slides, cautioning against interpreting concepts as direct biological measurements.
paper_title: CB-COMIL: interpretable prediction of melanoma immunotherapyresponse from multiplex immunofluorescence whole-slide images
